affSUP-desc:
Supremacy

The spirit has always been willing. The flesh has always been weak.—Comment, line 89, Category 2 bipedal locomotion protocol

A materialist ideology, believing that science is supreme and that technological progress must be prioritised above all else. They regard anything beyond scientific explanation as inherently useless, and their citizens readily replace flesh with machinery.

They blame childish religious wars and other failings of logic for the Great Mistake.
affHAR-desc:
Harmony

This world is a gift-garment that we wear upon ourselves and within ourselves, in gratitude to the giver.—From the Annunciation Rite of Polymorphalists

An ecologist ideology, believing that humanity must live in balance with nature, accepting limits on comfort and growth in the name of sustainability. Their citizens adapt themselves to the world rather than the world to themselves.

They blame over-industrialisation and the unsustainable nature of society for the Great Mistake.
affPUR-desc:
Purity

How much joy can this new world hold, when all I can think of is everything I've left behind?—Phaedra, Lamentation for Planetfall

A conservative ideology, believing that humanity must remain true to itself in both genetics and culture. Having lost so much, they cling to what remains of humanity's heritage, and see its preservation as the only way to stay human. Their citizens shun genetic modification and keep to traditional ways of life.

They blame the failure of long-held cultural values for the Great Mistake.
affNEU-desc:
Neutrality

Beware, you who seek first and final principles, for you are trampling in the garden of an angry God and he awaits you just beyond the last theorem.—Sister Mariam Godwinson, But For the Grace of God

Not all societies have fully committed to a single affinity. Undecided ideologies, spanning obscure schools of thought, take the best of all worlds. Their citizens may modify their bodies as they wish, though not to the same extent as the others, and their combat is built on ancient doctrines of movement rather than raw technological advantage.

Many undecided countries place their own interests ahead of grand ideological struggles, and view space colonisation as humanity's best bet for surviving the centuries to come.
affMAS-desc:
Mastery

We trusted the old world to hold. Never again will we trust what we did not build.—Aphorisms for Practical People

An environmental-engineering ideology, believing that humanity should have mastery over its surroundings. They seek to reshape ecosystems and make nature itself more resilient to our way of life.

They blame the fragility of the environment, and humanity's failure to adapt it to its will, for the Great Mistake.
affSYN-desc:
Synergy

Accepting the limitations of birthform betrays a lack of imagination.—Graffito within an abandoned city

An accelerationist ideology, believing that humanity must evolve and adapt to our new world, whatever the cost. Their citizens embrace radical change to both body and culture.

They blame unnecessarily conservative views of genetics and culture for preventing humanity from doing what needed to be done to avert the Great Mistake.
affDIV-desc:
Divinity

Go as I direct. Do as I bid. Why should my hand not control you? I see horizons you do not see. I make plans you cannot fathom.—Bhagavad 4

A spiritualist ideology, believing in the transcendence of the human mind and the importance of morality and ethics. They consider the spiritual and physical bodies separate entities, and so hold no strong feelings about genetics. Their societies are organised around faith and moral authority.

They blame rampant materialism and the rejection of faith and moral values for the Great Mistake.
